content: To accurately diagnose obesity, it is essential to calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) by measuring an individual's height and weight. In addition to BMI, other anthropometric measurements, such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio, should be assessed to better understand the distribution of body fat. These additional measurements are particularly valuable because they provide insights into the risk factors for cardiovascular and metabolic complications associated with obesity. Abdominal fat, in particular, is more strongly correlated with health risks compared to fat in other regions of the body. It is recommended that BMI and these supplementary measurements be monitored at least once a year to track any changes in obesity status. This regular monitoring allows for timely adjustments to treatment plans as needed.
